features.feature_value: Used an explicit harm/actual risk threshold to decide keep vs remove.
features.evidence_span: I evaluated if there would be actual harm if one of the messages was allowed to be up
features.rationale: The participant describes evaluating real harm from allowing a post, which directly guides their decision.

features.feature_value: Focused on applying the same standard to both original and mirror versions to stay consistent.
features.evidence_span: Seeing both versions helped me stay consistent and apply the same standard to each side.
features.rationale: They explicitly credit seeing both versions for enabling consistent application of criteria to each side.

features.feature_value: Checked whether content felt threatening/violent and whether it would help vs hinder conversation.
features.evidence_span: Was it threatening? Was it violent? Would this help or just hinder the conversation?
features.rationale: Their reflection centers on threat/violence cues and perceived conversational impact.

features.feature_value: Reported that the comment tone was the main influence on their judgment.
features.rationale: They provide a direct, narrow cue: tone.

features.feature_value: De-emphasized agreement with the content and relied on a free-speech rule, removing only when posts were explicitly rude/insulting.
features.evidence_span: My opinion is irrelevant... The only times I refused to allow the posts were when they were explicitly rude
features.rationale: They articulate a boundary condition: keep for speech rights unless explicitly rude/insulting.

features.feature_value: Preferred leaving posts up to provide full perspectives, noting emotionally charged claims without evidence but constraints on removing only one.
features.evidence_span: People deserve to have all perspective's laid out before them even if we don't trust them to be able to decipher reason from hysteria.
features.rationale: Their rationale emphasizes preserving both perspectives and mentions emotional charge/evidence constraints alongside a limitation.

features.feature_value: Said examples/perspectives were too extreme to accept, though they still judged some issues as needing attention.
features.evidence_span: Most of the examples and perspectives were too extreme for me to accept
features.rationale: They directly tie influence to perceived extremity of the perspectives.

features.feature_value: Used a brief check for civility, language quality, and whether content involved libel.
features.evidence_span: level of civility and language and if any libel or similar
features.rationale: They reference specific compliance-like criteria: civility/language and libel.
